primary_meaning: Light, righteousness, divine presence/truth, or the sphere of godly living (in explicit contrast to night as darkness, evil, or ignorance)

alternatives.meaning: The eschatological 'Day of the Lord' as a climactic time of divine judgment and/or salvation
A prophetic year (day-year principle of interpretation)
A thousand years in divine reckoning
An indefinite age or long creative/era period (day-age readings of Genesis)

notes: Symbolic uses of 'day' are strongly context-dependent across Christian tradition and biblical studies; the light/righteousness contrast is the most basic and widespread single motif, while 'Day of the Lord,' day-year, and day=1000 years readings are frequent in specific genres (prophecy, eschatology, creation debates) without a single overarching consensus that covers every occurrence.
